To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the GR is a constitutive transcription factor that controls many distinct cellular processes and that the specificity of GR-mediated transcriptional responses depends on context-dependent assembly of regulatory complexes at genomic sites.
the glucocorticoid (GC) receptor (GR) controls gene transcription via allostery and that this mechanism confers precision to its responses and plasticity in its actions.
the precision and plasticity of glucocorticoid hormone (GC)-induced gene transcription are conferred via allostery.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of the precision and plasticity of GR-mediated transcriptional regulation.
the mechanisms that underlie the precision and plasticity of GR-mediated responses, with an emphasis on the roles of allostery and combinatorial assembly.
understanding the structural and mechanistic basis for GR specificity, with a particular focus on the role of allostery in GR function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GR, as well as other TRFs, is an allosteric switch, a molecular device that is capable of integrating a multitude of signals, each contributing to the precision and plasticity of the response.
GR is an allosteric TRF, whose regulatory activity is controlled by multiple allostery-based processes.
allostery is a general mechanism for controlling TRF specificity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the precision of gene regulation is achieved through the combinatorial assembly of regulatory complexes that are determined by context-specific allosteric effects.

we have shown that GR is a transcription factor that is regulated at the level of its conformation, which in turn regulates its ability to interact with other proteins, including other transcription factors.
the GR is a highly versatile and dynamic transcription factor that is able to respond in a precise, context-dependent manner to multiple signals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GR conformational plasticity is a critical determinant of the diversity and precision of GR transcriptional regulatory networks.
TRFs are highly dynamic regulatory factors that integrate a wide variety of signals to control gene networks with exquisite specificity.

the molecular architecture of the GR is highly dynamic, and that the precise composition of GR-nucleating complexes, and thus the resulting transcriptional response, is determined by the integration of allosteric signals.
